questions.prompt: How is the promise "expires in one hour" stored and enforced in netpastebin? Explain what creation computes and which clock it uses (and why that matters for testing), the single comparison that is the whole feature, whether anything sweeps expired records and what that obliges every reader to do, and how the detail, raw and list paths each honor it.

keyPoints.text: Creation stores an absolute deadline, not a duration.
keyPoints.quote: Note what is stored: a *deadline*, not a duration.

keyPoints.text: The deadline comes from the injected TimeProvider, which makes expiry testable without waiting an hour.
keyPoints.quote: which is what makes expiry testable without waiting an hour.

keyPoints.text: IsExpired (ExpiresAt is set and is at or before now) is the whole expiry feature.
keyPoints.quote: This single expression is the whole expiry feature.

keyPoints.text: There is no background sweep: no timer, no hosted service, no cron.
keyPoints.quote: no timer, no hosted service, no cron.

keyPoints.text: Expiry is a read-time state transition: the record does not change and every reader must ask.
keyPoints.quote: the record does not change; every reader is obliged to ask.

keyPoints.text: So the guarantee is only as good as the discipline of each call site.
keyPoints.quote: the guarantee is only as good as the discipline of each call site.

keyPoints.text: The raw route reuses GetAsync, so detail and raw cannot disagree.
keyPoints.quote: the raw route reuses `GetAsync`, so the two cannot disagree.

keyPoints.text: ListAsync filters expired pastes, so search and pagination never show them and Total does not count them.
keyPoints.quote: so search and pagination never show an expired paste, and `Total` does not count it.

questions.prompt: What does netpastebin's expiry leave behind, and how well is it proven? Explain what happens to an expired paste's bytes and what "expires" therefore does and does not mean, its effect on the paste cap, which tier is the only executable evidence and what the xUnit suite contains, what inverting the IsExpired comparison showed, and what a backward clock jump does.

keyPoints.text: A read never rewrites the workspace, so the expired record stays in workspace-v1.json forever.
keyPoints.quote: a read does not rewrite the workspace, so the expired record remains in `workspace-v1.json` forever.

keyPoints.text: Expiry means unreadable through the API, not erased.
keyPoints.quote: means *unreadable through the API*, not *erased*.

keyPoints.text: Anyone who can read the data file can read the content.
keyPoints.quote: Anyone who can read the data file reads the content.

keyPoints.text: Expired records still count against the paste cap, so the workspace can fill with pastes nobody can see.
keyPoints.quote: A workspace can fill up with pastes nobody can see.

keyPoints.text: The console harness is the only executable evidence for expiry.
keyPoints.quote: the console harness is the only executable evidence

keyPoints.text: The xUnit suite that dotnet test runs contains no expiry test at all.
keyPoints.quote: contains no expiry test at all

keyPoints.text: Inverting the comparison in IsExpired leaves every test green.
keyPoints.quote: all tests stay green

keyPoints.text: A machine clock jumping backward un-expires pastes, and nothing checks for it.
keyPoints.quote: a machine whose clock jumps backward un-expires pastes.

questions.prompt: Explain two further invariant findings from the code tour. Size limits: what each of the three caps measures, how the same request can get different verdicts, and what tests pin the agreement. Content-type safety: how the raw endpoint, response headers and React rendering keep user content from being served executably, and the remaining gap.

keyPoints.text: Kestrel's MaxRequestBodySize limits the bytes of the JSON request.
keyPoints.quote: bytes of the JSON request.

keyPoints.text: The validator limits content to 100,000 characters (string length, i.e. UTF-16 chars).
The store limits the whole workspace document to 20 MiB.
keyPoints.quote: the whole workspace document ≤ 20 MiB

keyPoints.text: Escaped non-ASCII text can pass the validator's limit yet be rejected by Kestrel: same request, different verdict.
keyPoints.quote: same request, different verdict, depending on an escaping choice the user never made.

keyPoints.text: No test pins any agreement across the layers.
keyPoints.quote: No test pins any cross-layer agreement

keyPoints.text: The raw endpoint serves text/plain and every response carries nosniff, so a browser cannot sniff an HTML-shaped paste into a document.
keyPoints.quote: so a browser cannot sniff an HTML-shaped paste into a document

keyPoints.text: The React frontend renders paste content as text nodes.
keyPoints.quote: The React frontend renders content as text nodes

keyPoints.text: Gap: no tier asserts the nosniff header or the raw content type.
keyPoints.quote: nothing in any tier asserts the `nosniff` header or the raw content type
